ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a rectangle JKLM, with J at the upper left corner, K at the upper right corner, L at the lower right corner, and M at the lower left corner. The diagonals JL and MK are drawn in the figure, and they intersect at the interior point P. For this problem, it is necessary to focus on triangle JKL: JK is the upper side of the rectangle, KL is the right side, and JL is the diagonal from J to L. Reasoning: Because JKLM is a rectangle, adjacent sides JK and KL are perpendicular, therefore ∠JKL = 90°. The problem gives m∠KJL = 2x + 4, m∠JLK = 7x + 5. In triangle JKL, the sum of the three interior angles is 180°, so (2x + 4) + (7x + 5) + 90 = 180. Combining gives 9x + 99 = 180, therefore 9x = 81, x = 9.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the rectangle has top side JK horizontal, right side KL vertical, and diagonal JL running from the upper-left corner J to the lower-right corner L. Because the horizontal and vertical sides of a rectangle are perpendicular, the angle a line makes with the horizontal and the angle it makes with the vertical are complementary. Therefore, (2x + 4) + (7x + 5) = 90. Solve 9x + 9 = 90, giving x = 9.
